rows.what: One line in your own words (pull quote)
rows.copy: Established in 2009, we grew our love for seventeen years.

They met in college and became best friends, the kind who trade records, sketchbooks, and unsolicited opinions. Somewhere between the music and the art, the thing they shared most turned out to be a refusal to be anyone but themselves. The first kiss came at The Showdown Saloon in San Marcos in 2009, and they have been together ever since. Seventeen years later, they are gathering the people they love to make it official and join two families. Dressed in black, naturally.
Find a seat; the rite begins at four. A small chapel, and a small circle of witnesses.
3:30–3:50 pm · Guests arrive; we’ll take photos as you come in
4:05 pm · The ceremony, about forty minutes
4:45 pm · We leave the chapel together
Tell your GPS “County Road,” not “Country Road.”
A buffet supper, a pour-your-own bar, cake, music, and the salt bowl. The sun sets at 5:31; bring a layer.
6:00 pm · Buffet dinner and the salt bowl
About 25 minutes from the chapel. No shuttle; free parking on site and on the street.
Go gently. Take the long way home.

rows.what: End of night schedule item 1 (time · detail)

rows.copy: Salt preserves. For as long as people have made promises, it has sealed them. At the reception, a bowl of salt will be waiting. Bring a small totem that speaks to you to add to it, and with it a piece of wisdom for the marriage: a blessing, a toast, a memory, a warning, a recipe. Once everyone has a plate, we’ll gather, and you’re invited to say yours aloud. The bowl stays out all night; add to it whenever you’re moved. It goes home with them and keeps.
Come in your most fabulous black ensemble.
Evenings fall into the low 40s, and much of the day is spent outdoors. Bring layers for comfort, ideally ones you won’t mind being photographed in.
We wish for everyone to be fully present during the ceremony. While we appreciate the gesture to document this day, we’ve got it taken care of with a wonderfully talented photographer.
About thirty witnesses. Plus-ones only if named on the invitation.
There are no room blocks; book wherever suits you. Some guests are staying at the Hilton Garden Inn in Cedar Park.
Hilton Garden Inn Cedar Park Austin
Where some of the other guests are staying.
On the San Gabriel River at Rivery Park, near the historic square. Closest to the chapel.
A historic bed and breakfast in Georgetown, across from Southwestern University.
Practical, and between the two venues.
A motor-court hotel at The Domain in north Austin.
Quiet and old-world in west Austin (formerly Hotel Granduca).
Driving back to San Marcos that night? It's about an hour south on I-35.
Between 3:30 and 3:50. We’ll be taking photos as guests arrive, and everyone is seated by 4:00.
Can I bring a plus-one or my children?
This is a small, intimate wedding, and the venues are small too: plus-ones only if they’re named on your invitation.
Your presence is the gift. If you insist, a note for the bowl.
The chapel has twenty guest spaces inside the gate, with accessible spaces closer to the door. La Villa Rosa has free parking on site and on the street.
The chapel has a gentle-slope entry and accessible restrooms about fifty feet away. Not every area of La Villa Rosa is wheelchair accessible; tell us what you need and we’ll make it work.
How do I get between venues?
By car, about 25 minutes. There’s no shuttle, so plan to drive or share a ride.

Casey Eickhoff, the Maid of Honor, can answer anything in our stead. Before the day, write to caseyisonit@gmail.com with “Meg + Ryan wedding” in the subject. On the day itself, email goes unchecked; Casey will share a number for texting with you directly.
Drinks are provided, and there’s a pour-your-own bar. If you have a drink of choice, you’re welcome to bring it.
There’s a pool at La Villa Rosa with no lifeguard on duty, and a white horse and a small goat roam the property. Please be kind to the animals.
Reply by the twenty-second of November.
It is done. Your name is in the book. We'll see you at the chapel.
You'll be missed. We'll keep a pinch of salt in your name.
